newsitem.title: RUSSIA: AGROKHLEB-Russian sunseed output seen flat or up.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB-Russian sunseed output seen flat or up.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union.
RUSSIAN SUNSEED AREA 3.5 MLN HECTARES, 10 PCT DOWN ON '96;
OUTPUT PROVISIONALLY SEEN FLAT OR UP TO 2.7-3.2 MLN T
MOSCOW, June 23 - At this early stage, SovEcon forecasts Russia's total 1997 sunseed output at 2.7-3.2 million tonnes, close to last year's poor crop of 2.75 million tonnes.
SovEcon's estimate for Russia's total sunseed area remain virtually unchanged in the range of 3.50-3.55 million hectares.
Though this would be a decline on 1995 and 1996 levels, it would nonetheless be Russia's third record-highest level of sunseed plantings (Table 2).
We expect a decline in sunseed plantings in most regions, except for Voronezh and Tambov Oblasts (Central-Chernozem region).
Delayed planting may result in a decline in yields and oil content, particularly if adverse weather is present during the harvest.

Despite an early start in sunseed sowings in the Central-Chernozem (Black Earth) region and the North Caucasus, cool weather in late April and May seriously slowed down sowing progress, particularly in the North Caucasus.
